: SCHEDULE :
 ALL THAT PIECE AND PARCEL OF PROPERTY BEARING SURVEY NO.33 SITUATED AT BHOOPASANDRA VILLAGE,
KASABA HOBLI, BANGALORE NORTH TALUK, BANGALORE TO AN EXTENT OF 02 ACRES 07 GUNTAS BOUNDED ON:
 EAST BY : SURVEY NO.13,
 WEST BY : CART ROAD,
 NORTH BY : SY.NO.34  SOUTH BY : JABBAR SHERIFF'S PROPERTY.
 THIS PETITION HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 04.10.2023 FOR ORDERS AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners have filed this writ petition seeking a declaration that the preliminary notification dated 19.01.1978 and the final notification dated 28.12.1982 for formation of 'Rajamahal Vilas II Stage Layout' and the scheme has lapsed in terms of Section 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 (hereinafter referred to as 'BDA', for short) and also in terms of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 2013', for short), and they seek certain other directions.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that although 131 acres 33 guntas were notified for acquisition in the preliminary notification bearing No.A3 TR (S) SLAO/BDA/77-78 dated 19.01.1978, for the formation of RMV II Stage Layout, however, in the final notification it was reduced to 108 acres 17 guntas.
Further, possession of only 69 acres 28 guntas is said to have been taken.
Nevertheless, factually, the layout is formed in an extent of 13 acres 34 guntas only.
It is contended that although in the records of the BDA 234 sites are formed, however, only 132 sites were allotted.

Janardhan vs State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89881776/
4 3.

It is contended that having regard to all these factual aspects, in WP No.53124-126/2015, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court allowed the writ petition by order dated 05.02.2016 while declaring that the scheme was not substantially implemented as was declared earlier by a Division Bench of this Court in the case of Dr. A. Parthasarathy and others vs. State of Karnataka & Others, reported in ILR 2017 KAR 3489.

entities.text: Dr. A. Parthasarathy and others vs. State of Karnataka & Others, reported in ILR 2017 KAR 3489
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of the respondent - BDA that a layout has been formed and sites have been allotted to various persons

was rejected while holding that even if any allotments were made, the only remedy to the persons claiming such allotment would be to claim appropriate relief against the BDA in appropriate proceedings.
It was held that such allotment would not efface the legal provisions or the effect of the legal provisions as held by the Division Bench.
It is submitted that the case of the petitioners is squarely covered by the said decision.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent - BDA submitted that the award amount of Rs.2,97,705/- in respect of 5 acres 8 guntas in Sy.No.33 has been deposited in the revenue deposit.
The claim of the petitioners is in respect of 2 acres 7 guntas out of 5 acres 8 guntas.
In that view of the matter, it is contended that there cannot be a declaration that a part of the scheme is implemented and the other portions are unimplemented.
Moreover, it is contended that sites have been formed in the land in question and the same have been allotted to various persons.

Therefore,
it would be untenable on the part of the petitioners to contend that the scheme is not substantially implemented.

It is brought to the notice of this Court that in a subsequent judgment, another Division Bench, in the case of A. Chandrashekhar and another Vs. State and others reported in 2020 (1) Kar. L.J. 866 the earlier decision in the case of A. Partha Sarthy (supra) (which was referred to by the learned counsel for the petitioners) was noticed, but the acquisition proceedings were upheld.

entities.text: A. Chandrashekhar and another Vs. State and others reported in 2020 (1) Kar. L.J. 866
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having regard to the contentions of the petitioners regarding applicability of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013, it was contended that in a subsequent decision, in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal and others reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that once the land vested in the State free from all encumbrances, it cannot be divested and the proceedings under the Act would not lapse, even if award is not made within the statutorily stipulated period.
5.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal and others reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it has been admitted by the respondent - BDA that it has not been able to trace the original records to substantiate the fact that the award amount was deposited in revenue deposit.

It has been admitted that the respondent - BDA is not in a position to place material before this Court either to evidence deposit of the award amount or of payment made to the petitioners/ their predecessors-in-title.

6. During the course of these proceedings, sufficient opportunity was given to the respondent - BDA to place material before this Court to satisfy the Court regarding the deposit and payment of the award amount to the predecessors-in-title of the petitioners.
A suggestion was also made to the respondent - BDA to allot alternative sites to the petitioners in lieu of the respondent - BDA forming the sites and utilizing the lands of the petitioners.
But, the respondent - BDA was unable to produce the original records evidencing the deposit or payment of the award amount.
The learned counsel for the respondent - BDA submitted that it is not in a position to allot alternative sites to the petitioners.

Janardhan vs State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89881776/
5 7.

The learned counsel for the writ petitioners has contended that in many such cases, having regard to the contentions of the respondent - BDA that it has formed layout and allotted sites to various persons, this Court has directed the respondent - BDA to allot alternative lands of similar value or allot developed lands having regard to the value of the utilized lands.

The decisions cited by the learned counsel are W.P.No.45695/2011 dated - 10 - 26.07.2012 in Dr. R. Arunachalam Vs. Bangalore Development Authority and another and W.P.
No.46259/2013 and connected matters, disposed of on 16.09.2014 in Sri. A.M. Hanumanthe Gowda Vs. Bangalore Development Authority and another.

entities.text: Dr. R. Arunachalam Vs. Bangalore Development Authority and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sri. A.M. Hanumanthe Gowda Vs. Bangalore Development Authority and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such orders have been confirmed at the hands of the Division Bench.

8. Having regard to the fact that the respondent - BDA is not in a position to place on record any material to show deposit of the award amount or payment, this Court is of the considered opinion that the writ petitioners are entitled for relief.

Consequently, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.
ii) It is hereby declared that the scheme for formation of 'Rajamahal Vilas II Stage Layout' insofar as 2 acres 7 guntas belonging to the - 11 - petitioners, in Sy.No.33 of Bhupasandra village, Kasba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk is concerned,
is declared as lapsed in terms of Section 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976.

iii) However, since it is contended by the respondent - BDA that it has utilized the scheduled lands for formation of the layout, it is hereby directed that the respondent - BDA shall initiate acquisition proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013 and pay compensation together with all benefits,
interest, etc., to the petitioners in respect of the scheduled land OR;
iv) Allot alternative land equivalent to the market value of the scheduled lands OR;
v) Allot developed lands/sites equivalent to the market value of the scheduled lands.
- 12 - vi) The entire exercise shall be completed as expeditiously as possible and at any rate within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
